title: Programme
text:
Session types
The programme combines invited keynotes, contributed presentations, and collaborative breakout sessions:

Keynotes have a 45-minute slot and set the stage for the discussion of the day.
Presentations are contributed talks of roughly 20 minutes each.
Breakout sessions are the core of the workshop. In parallel sessions, small groups work on the four research directions, with the goal of critically assessing progress since the original priority research directions and identifying open challenges.
Presentation of breakout findings brings the groups back together to report their results to all participants.
Organisational and collaborative slots — session overview, session alignment, status sync, final result preparation, and the social event — are used to coordinate between the groups and to prepare the joint outcome of the workshop.

The findings collected during the breakout sessions form the basis of the joint scientific article that will be prepared after the workshop.

title: SciML Frontiers: Progress, Evolution, and Future Directions — Workshop 2026
text:
22–23 September 2026 • Augsburg, Germany



Scientific Machine Learning (SciML), the fusion of scientific computing and machine learning algorithms, has proven to be a transformative force in academia and is rapidly establishing a firm foothold in industrial applications. The foundational 2018 SciML workshop outlined six priority research directions (PRDs) for the nascent field of SciML, anchoring future development around critical pillars such as domain awareness, robustness, and interpretability. The SciML landscape has evolved profoundly over the past seven years. Considering these advancements, this workshop, hosted by the Centre for Advanced Analytics and Predictive Sciences at the University of Augsburg, convenes researchers from diverse disciplines to re-evaluate the original priorities within the context of current technological frontiers. Through expert keynotes, technical presentations, and collaborative breakout sessions, participants will share practical insights and critically analyse current progress and emerging challenges within the field. Our primary objective is to assess the trajectory of the original PRDs and collaboratively shape the future research agenda for SciML. The insights generated during this two-day event will be synthesised into a comprehensive scientific article, targeting high-impact journals such as Nature Machine Intelligence or Neurocomputing.
We have synthesised the original six PRDs into four focused research directions, which participants will explore deeply during the breakout sessions.





Numerical Foundation of SciML


Discretisation, Stability and Convergence







Beyond prediction


Control, Optimisation and Application







Automation and Scalability in SciML


From Prototype to Production Scale







Domain Awareness and Interpretability


Physical Priors, Explainability and Trust




The event is organised by Prof. Lars Mikelsons, Prof. Michael Schlottke-Lakemper and Andreas Hofmann (see Organisers), and is hosted by the Centre for Advanced Analytics and Predictive Sciences at the University of Augsburg.
